lesson.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

sources.title: Code Your Own CLI With Rust

steps.title: Initialize project and add clap
steps.instructions: Run cargo new bestls in the empty workdir and cd into bestls. Open Cargo.toml and add clap with the derive feature under [dependencies].

targets.caption: Add the clap crate with the derive feature under [dependencies]

hints: Run cargo new bestls in your workspace directory and cd into it.
Open Cargo.toml and locate the [dependencies] section.
Add clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] } under [dependencies].
common_mistakes: Forgetting to enable the derive feature on clap, which prevents deriving Parser later.
Running commands outside the new project directory.

steps.title: Define CLI struct and parse arguments
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs, define a struct deriving Debug and Parser with #[command(version, about)] and an Option<PathBuf> field, then call parse() in main(). Run cargo run -- --help to see the generated usage.

targets.caption: Define the CLI struct with Parser and command attributes

explanations.topic: Passing arguments after -- in cargo run

hints: Import Parser from clap and PathBuf from std::path.
Decorate struct CLI with #[derive(Debug, Parser)] and #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")].
Call CLI::parse() inside main(), then run cargo run -- --help.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the -- separator in cargo run -- --help, which passes --help to cargo instead of your binary.
Omitting version inside #[command(...)] so --version is not generated.
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best Ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); }

steps.title: Check path existence with colored errors
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors to Cargo.toml, unwrap cli.path with a default of ".", and check fs::exists(&path) in src/main.rs to print red error messages when the path is missing or unreadable. Test with cargo run -- nonexistent.

targets.caption: Check if the path exists and colorize errors

hints: Use cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to default to the current directory.
Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml and import owo_colors::OwoColorize.
Match fs::exists(&path) with if let Ok(does_exist) and print colored errors with .red().
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import owo_colors::OwoColorize, causing .red() not to be found.
Treating fs::exists(&path) as returning a bool instead of io::Result<bool>.
steps.code: let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")); if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } } else { println!("{}", "error reading directory".red()); }

steps.title: Read and print directory filenames
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs, write a get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> function that uses fs::read_dir(path) to collect filenames, then print each entry from main(). Run cargo run to list the current directory.

targets.caption: Implement get_files to read entries from the directory

hints: Import std::path::Path and create fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String>.
Iterate over fs::read_dir(path) and unwrap each Result entry with if let Ok(file) = entry.
In main(), loop for file in get_files(&path) and print each filename.
common_mistakes: Passing PathBuf instead of &Path to get_files(&path).
Calling file.file_name() without converting OsString via .into_string().
steps.code: fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Collect metadata into FileEntry structs
steps.instructions: Add strum and strum_macros to Cargo.toml, define EntryType and FileEntry, and update get_files to build entries from fs::metadata(file.path()). Run cargo run to see the FileEntry debug output.

targets.caption: Add strum with derive feature and strum_macros
Read fs::metadata for each file path

explanations.topic: Using strum Display macro on enums

hints: Add strum = { version = "0.27", features = ["derive"] } and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml.
Define enum EntryType { File, Dir } deriving Debug and Display, plus struct FileEntry.
Use fs::metadata(file.path()) (not &path) so each file reports its own size and type.
common_mistakes: Passing &path instead of file.path() to fs::metadata(), which reads the directory metadata for every entry.
Forgetting to update the return type of get_files from Vec<String> to Vec<FileEntry>.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String, }

steps.title: Format directory output as colored table
steps.instructions: Add tabled to Cargo.toml, derive Tabled on your file entry struct, and build a styled Table in main() with rounded borders and colors. Run cargo run to inspect the table.

targets.caption: Run cargo run to see the table

hints: Import Table, Tabled, settings::Style, and settings::object::{Columns, Rows} plus Color from tabled.
Add #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] to FileEntry and #[tabled(rename="...")] attributes to its fields.
Make table mutable (let mut table = Table::new(...)) so .with() and .modify() can mutate it.
common_mistakes: Importing Style or Color from owo_colors or clap instead of tabled::settings.
Forgetting to mark table as mut before calling table.with(...) and table.modify(...).
steps.code: let get_files = get_files(&path); let mut table = Table::new(get_files); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modified timestamps with chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono to Cargo.toml and convert meta.modified() into DateTime<Utc> formatted as "%a %b %e %Y" in your mapping function. Run cargo run -- src to test.
hints: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml and import chrono::{DateTime, Utc}.
Inside map_data, match meta.modified() with if let Ok(modi) and convert it via let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into();.
Format the date using date.format("%a %b %e %Y") and fall back to String::default().
common_mistakes: Using the reserved keyword mod as a variable name instead of modi.
Forgetting to update Columns::one(3) to Color::FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW.
steps.code: modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() }

steps.title: Add JSON output flag with serde
steps.instructions: Add #[arg(short, long)] json: bool to your Cli struct, add serde (with derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, and derive Serialize on your entry structs. When cli.json is true, print serde_json::to_string of the file list, then run cargo run -- -j to see the JSON output.

targets.caption: Add serde with derive feature and serde_json = "1.0"
Serialize the file list to JSON when cli.json is true

hints: Decorate json: bool in struct CLI with #[arg(short, long)] so -j and --json work.
Add serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } and serde_json = "1.0" to Cargo.toml, and derive Serialize on both EntryType and FileEntry.
Branch on cli.json in main() to call serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path)) or print_table(path).
common_mistakes: Deriving Serialize on FileEntry without also deriving Serialize on EntryType.
Omitting #[arg(short, long)] on json: bool, which makes clap treat it as a required positional argument.
steps.code: #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, if cli.json { let get_files = get_files(&path); println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(path); }
